title: International Ovarian Tumor Analysis (IOTA) Simple Rules risque évaluation
abbreviations: International Ovarian Tumor Analysis (IOTA) Simple Rules Risk Assessment
formula:
The model coefficients to calculate the risk of malignancy in adnexal masses are as follows:

| Variable | Coefficient |
| --- | --- |
| Intercept | -0.97 |
| B1 (unilocular cyst) | -3.41 |
| B2 (solid components present, but <7 mm) | -2.25 |
| B3 (acoustic shadows) | -1.66 |
| B4 (smooth multilocular tumor with largest diameter <100 mm) | -2.75 |
| B5 (no blood flow; color score 1) | -1.86 |
| M1 (irregular solid tumor) | 2.19 |
| M2 (ascites) | 2.65 |
| M3 (at least 4 papillary structures) | 1.53 |
| M4 (irregular multilocular solid tumor with largest diameter ≥100 mm) | 0.98 |
| M5 (very strong flow; color score 4) | 1.55 |
| Ultrasound examination at oncology center | 0.92 |

Risk of malignancy, % = [e^x^/(1 + e^x^)]*100,

where x = Σ(β*variable)

how_to_use.why:
- The original Simple Rules study provided a list of 5 benign characteristics and 5 malignant characteristics. An ultrasound report was classified as malignant or benign if findings met all 5 characteristics in one of the groups.
- Ultrasound reports which showed a mix of these characteristics were classified as “indeterminate” which limited the score’s clinical use.
- Study authors created a logistic regression model in 2016 and added another input; the location where the ultrasound imaging was performed. This enhanced model with risk calculation is what MDCalc has chosen to include.
how_to_use.when:
- In patients who are undergoing adnexal surgery.
- Not for use in patients who are being treated with observation or other conservative measures.
how_to_use.pearls:
- L’utilisation de ce score nécessite que l’utilisateur comprenne la terminologie et les constatations échographiques.
- Pour des définitions supplémentaires des caractéristiques d’imagerie décrites dans ce score, voir le rapport du groupe IOTA [ici](https://www.iotagroup.org/sites/default/files/Timmerman_et_al_UOG_2000.pdf).

next_steps.management:
- M features are more closely associated with malignancy while B features are more associated with a benign tumor.
- The presence of M features increases the risk of a tumor being malignant while the presence of B features will decrease the risk.
- Use as part of presurgical counseling and planning with your patient. Remember to only use this score in patients who are undergoing surgery.
